_comment: Bundled vocabulary for the findings-ingest validator (contract requirement 3).
Kept in sync with contract/findings-ingest.schema.json by scripts/check_repo.py.
These are the SHAPES an ingested result can take — the report formats this piece reads, the
classes of scanner it accepts, and the severity/status/category values Noru's own API publishes
for a security finding. They are not framework content: no control text, no remediation window,
no deadline. What is already open, which assets and risks exist and when a risk's treatment is
due all come from the customer's organization at scan time, never from this file. See
severity, status and category are the published enums for a Noru security finding. Their source
is the 'Security Findings' entry in the Canonical Values Reference of
https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt. Do not extend them here: a value this piece invents is a value
the API rejects at push time, which is the worst moment to find out.
_class_category_comment: The category a finding of each class is filed under by default. A person may file one under
another category in the manifest; this is only what the skeleton proposes.
_scanner_severity_comment: How a scanner's own rating becomes the severity the skeleton proposes. A numeric score is read
on the CVSS v3 qualitative scale (critical from 9.0, high from 7.0, medium from 4.0, low above
0); a SARIF level is read as below. The result is a proposal, as it is in every other piece:
how bad a finding is HERE is the person's call, written into the manifest.
_status_horizon_days_comment: How long an interpretation of a finding may stand, counted in days from the day the result was
observed. This is not a remediation deadline and must never be read as one: it says when
somebody has to look at the judgement again. A deadline is whatever the treatment of the linked
risk says in Noru, and this piece sets none.
An open or in-progress finding is a live observation that the next scan refreshes, so the
window is short. Accepting a finding, or calling it a false positive, is a human decision to
leave the code as it is — it gets a longer window, but never an unbounded one.
